Definition: adverb from a compound of the base of G3674 and G2372; unanimously:--with one accord (mind).
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says homothymadón, it means with one accord (mind). The word appears 11 times, and in Acts and Romans it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: homothymadón matters to me because one accord is the Spirit’s work — the church prayed, ate and gave with one heart. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
RelatedEvents: Pentecost; The Believers Pray for Boldness
